stimulus.title: A pond in winter
stimulus.text: PLACEHOLDER content, written only to test the free-response pages; it has had no accuracy check. In winter a layer of ice forms on the surface of a pond, while the water at the bottom stays liquid at about 4 °C.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe how hydrogen bonds are arranged in ice compared with liquid water.

rubric.point: In ice, each molecule is held in a stable, open lattice by hydrogen bonds; in liquid water the bonds constantly break and re-form.
accept: fixed open lattice in ice, shifting bonds in liquid

parts.sample: In ice, hydrogen bonds hold each molecule in a fixed, open lattice. In liquid water the hydrogen bonds keep breaking and re-forming.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why ice is less dense than liquid water.

rubric.point: The open lattice spaces molecules farther apart than in the liquid, so the same mass takes up more volume.
accept: molecules farther apart in the lattice

parts.sample: The lattice holds molecules farther apart than in liquid water, so a given mass of ice takes up more space and is less dense.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain how the ice layer affects the temperature of the water below it.

rubric.point: Floating ice insulates the water below, slowing heat loss to the cold air.
accept: ice acts as an insulating layer

parts.sample: The floating ice insulates the water underneath, so less heat escapes to the cold air and the deeper water stays liquid.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Predict what would happen to fish in the pond if ice were denser than liquid water, and justify your prediction.

rubric.point: Ice would sink and the pond could freeze from the bottom up, leaving fish without liquid water.

parts.sample: Ice would sink as it formed, so the pond could freeze from the bottom up and the fish would lose the liquid water they need.
